newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Divided Israel united in backing Clinton - poll.
newsitem.headline: Divided Israel united in backing Clinton - poll.

text.p: If Israelis -- politically divided at home -- could vote in the U.S. presidential election, only five percent would cast their ballots for Republican challenger Bob Dole, opinion polls showed on Friday.

Bill Clinton, dubbed by the local media as the Jewish state's best friend, would take between 85 and 87 percent of the "Israeli" vote, according to the polls in the Maariv and Yedioth Ahronoth newspapers.

Clinton, a driving force in Middle East peace efforts, won over Israelis with his "Shalom, friend" eulogy for assassinated Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin a year ago and by rushing to Israel after a wave of Moslem militant suicide bombings last March.
The Gallup poll in Maariv surveyed 505 Israeli Jews and the Dahaf poll in Yedioth Ahronoth questioned 503. Their margins of error were four percent.
